Number of Required Key Personnel    4

Description of Services

Fisheries laboratories play a critical role in ensuring the safety, quality, and compliance of fish and aquatic products for both domestic consumption and international trade. These labs conduct testing for contaminants, microbiological hazards, chemical residues, and other parameters to meet sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) measures and technical trade barriers (TBT)requirements. However, most fisheries and aquaculture laboratories in Tanzania lack accreditation to international standards like ISO/IEC 17025, limiting their credibility and capacity to support regulatory enforcement, trade, and public health, which specifies general requirements for the competence of testing and calibration laboratories. This gap hinders trade facilitation, increases costs, and limits market access.
This TOR outlines consultancy services to assist Fisheries Quality and Control, NMRC, and TAFIRI Laboratories in achieving ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation, focusing on method validation, proficiency testing, and overall quality management system implementation to meet global quality and safetyrequirements, enhancing the credibility of test results for fish health, waterquality, and fishery product safety, and facilitating international trade.

Scope of Activity

1.0 Scope of the Consultancy
The consultant shall provide comprehensive technical support to selected fisheries and aquaculture laboratories in Tanzania to achieve ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation. The scope of work includes five interlinked components:
1.1.Baseline Assessment and Gap Analysis
·Conduct diagnostic assessments of laboratory infrastructure, equipment, staffing, and existing quality systems.
·Review current analytical methods, SOPs, documentation practices, and internal controls.
·Identify gaps in compliance with ISO/IEC 17025 requirements
·Produce a detailed gap analysis report with prioritized recommendations.

1.2.Method Validation
·Assessment of Current Methods: Review existing analytical methods used in fisheries laboratories for testing fish and fishery products (e.g.microbiological, chemical, and physical parameters), water quality, and fish health assessments.
·Method Development and Validation:
oIdentify priority analytical methods based on national fisheries and aquaculture needs, such as total plate count, coliforms, heavy metals, pesticide residues, and fish disease diagnostics, ensuring compliance with ISO/IEC 17025.
oValidate methods for accuracy, precision, specificity, sensitivity, and measurement uncertainty, following international guidelines (e.g., WHO Good Practices for Pharmaceutical Quality Control Laboratories).
oDevelop validation protocols covering accuracy, precision, specificity, linearity, limit of detection (LOD), and limit of quantification (LOQ)
oConduct method validation trials in collaboration with laboratory staff
·Documentation: Prepare detailed standard operating procedures (SOPs), validation protocols, and reports for all validated methods.
·Training: Train laboratory staff on validated methods, including calibration, maintenance of equipment, and record-keeping.
1.3.Design and Implementation of Proficiency Testing (PT)
·Design PT Schemes: Develop proficiency testing programs tailored to fisheries

laboratories, focusing on parameters relevant to fish and fishery products, water quality, and fish health (e.g., viral and bacterial pathogens, chemical contaminants).
·Sample Preparation and Distribution: Coordinate the preparation and distribution of standardized samples to participating laboratories, ensuring confidentiality and compliance with ISO/IEC 17043 standards.
·Performance Evaluation: Analyze PT results, provide feedback reports to laboratories, and recommend corrective actions to improve performance.
·Inter-Laboratory Comparisons: Facilitate inter-laboratory comparisons within Tanzania and, where feasible, with regional or international laboratories to benchmark performance.
1.4.Quality Management System (QMS) Development
·Develop or revise laboratory quality manuals, SOPs, work instructions, and record-keeping templates.
·Establish systems for document control, equipment calibration, maintenance, traceability, and corrective/preventive actions to international standards.
·Train laboratory personnel on QMS implementation, internal audits, and continual improvement
·Support labs in conducting mock audits and management reviews

1.5 ISO/IEC 17025 Accreditation
·Accreditation Support:
oAssisting selecting an accredited body (e.g., SADCAS or SANAS) and preparing for accreditation assessments.
oGuide laboratories through the ISO/IEC 17025 application process with recognized accreditation bodies (e.g., SADCAS, TBS, SANAS)
oLiaise with accreditation assessors and regulatory authorities as needed
oSupport laboratories during accreditation audits and address findings to achieve certification.
·Post-Accreditation Maintenance: Develop a plan for maintaining accreditation, including regular internal audits, management reviews, and participation in Schemes.
1.6. Capacity Building
·Staff Training: Conduct workshops and hands-on training for laboratory analysts and managers on method validation, PT, and QMS implementation.

·Infrastructure Assessment: Evaluate laboratory facilities and recommend upgrades to meet ISO/IEC 17025 requirements (e.g., equipment calibration, environmental controls).
·Sustainability Plan: Develop a roadmap for sustained laboratory improvement, including strategies for continuous training and equipment maintenance.

Description of Services

Fisheries laboratories play a critical role in ensuring the safety, quality, and compliance of fish and aquatic products for both domestic consumption and international trade. These labs conduct testing for contaminants, microbiological hazards, chemical residues, and other parameters to meet sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) measures and technical trade barriers (TBT)requirements. However, most fisheries and aquaculture laboratories in Tanzania lack accreditation to international standards like ISO/IEC 17025, limiting their credibility and capacity to support regulatory enforcement, trade, and public health, which specifies general requirements for the competence of testing and calibration laboratories. This gap hinders trade facilitation, increases costs, and limits market access.
This TOR outlines consultancy services to assist Fisheries Quality and Control, NMRC, and TAFIRI Laboratories in achieving ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation, focusing on method validation, proficiency testing, and overall quality management system implementation to meet global quality and safetyrequirements, enhancing the credibility of test results for fish health, waterquality, and fishery product safety, and facilitating international trade.

Scope of Activity

1.0 Scope of the Consultancy
The consultant shall provide comprehensive technical support to selected fisheries and aquaculture laboratories in Tanzania to achieve ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation. The scope of work includes five interlinked components:
1.1.Baseline Assessment and Gap Analysis
·Conduct diagnostic assessments of laboratory infrastructure, equipment, staffing, and existing quality systems.
·Review current analytical methods, SOPs, documentation practices, and internal controls.
·Identify gaps in compliance with ISO/IEC 17025 requirements
·Produce a detailed gap analysis report with prioritized recommendations.

1.2.Method Validation
·Assessment of Current Methods: Review existing analytical methods used in fisheries laboratories for testing fish and fishery products (e.g.microbiological, chemical, and physical parameters), water quality, and fish health assessments.
·Method Development and Validation:
oIdentify priority analytical methods based on national fisheries and aquaculture needs, such as total plate count, coliforms, heavy metals, pesticide residues, and fish disease diagnostics, ensuring compliance with ISO/IEC 17025.
oValidate methods for accuracy, precision, specificity, sensitivity, and measurement uncertainty, following international guidelines (e.g., WHO Good Practices for Pharmaceutical Quality Control Laboratories).
oDevelop validation protocols covering accuracy, precision, specificity, linearity, limit of detection (LOD), and limit of quantification (LOQ)
oConduct method validation trials in collaboration with laboratory staff
·Documentation: Prepare detailed standard operating procedures (SOPs), validation protocols, and reports for all validated methods.
·Training: Train laboratory staff on validated methods, including calibration, maintenance of equipment, and record-keeping.
1.3.Design and Implementation of Proficiency Testing (PT)
·Design PT Schemes: Develop proficiency testing programs tailored to fisheries

laboratories, focusing on parameters relevant to fish and fishery products, water quality, and fish health (e.g., viral and bacterial pathogens, chemical contaminants).
·Sample Preparation and Distribution: Coordinate the preparation and distribution of standardized samples to participating laboratories, ensuring confidentiality and compliance with ISO/IEC 17043 standards.
·Performance Evaluation: Analyze PT results, provide feedback reports to laboratories, and recommend corrective actions to improve performance.
·Inter-Laboratory Comparisons: Facilitate inter-laboratory comparisons within Tanzania and, where feasible, with regional or international laboratories to benchmark performance.
1.4.Quality Management System (QMS) Development
·Develop or revise laboratory quality manuals, SOPs, work instructions, and record-keeping templates.
·Establish systems for document control, equipment calibration, maintenance, traceability, and corrective/preventive actions to international standards.
·Train laboratory personnel on QMS implementation, internal audits, and continual improvement
·Support labs in conducting mock audits and management reviews

1.5 ISO/IEC 17025 Accreditation
·Accreditation Support:
oAssisting selecting an accredited body (e.g., SADCAS or SANAS) and preparing for accreditation assessments.
oGuide laboratories through the ISO/IEC 17025 application process with recognized accreditation bodies (e.g., SADCAS, TBS, SANAS)
oLiaise with accreditation assessors and regulatory authorities as needed
oSupport laboratories during accreditation audits and address findings to achieve certification.
·Post-Accreditation Maintenance: Develop a plan for maintaining accreditation, including regular internal audits, management reviews, and participation in Schemes.
1.6. Capacity Building
·Staff Training: Conduct workshops and hands-on training for laboratory analysts and managers on method validation, PT, and QMS implementation.

·Infrastructure Assessment: Evaluate laboratory facilities and recommend upgrades to meet ISO/IEC 17025 requirements (e.g., equipment calibration, environmental controls).
·Sustainability Plan: Develop a roadmap for sustained laboratory improvement, including strategies for continuous training and equipment maintenance.

Assignment Title: Request for expression of interest for Consultancy Services to provide readiness and incubation support to Community groups and Champions earmarked for support under the TRALARD II Project in Copperbelt, Muchinga and Southern provinces.

Reference No.: ZM-MGEE-553248-CS-QCBS

The Government of the Republic of Zambia through the Ministry of Green Economy and Environment (MGEE) has received financing from the World Bank, Climate Investment Funds (CIF), Global Environmental Facility (GEF), Least Developed Countries Fund (LDCF), Nordic Development Fund and Scaling Climate Action by Lowering Emissions (SCALE) totaling USD 137 million to support the implementation of the Transforming Landscapes for Resilience and Development (TRALARD) II project in Copperbelt, Luapula, Muchinga, Northern and Southern provinces, and intends to apply part of the funds towards eligible payments under three contracts for Consultancy Services to provide readiness and incubation support to Community groups and Champions earmarked for support under the TRALARD II Project according to the following three (3) lots:

Lot No.

Provinces

Target Districts

1

Southern

Chirundu, Siavonga, Gwembe, Sinazongwe, and Pemba

2

Southern

Kazungula, Kalomo, Namwala, Monze, and Itezhi-tezhi

3

Copperbelt & Muchinga

Lufwanyama, Masaiti, Mpongwe, Mufulira, Lavushimanda and Mpika

The objective of the assignment is to strengthen the capacity of beneficiary community groups and champions to effectively identify and manage their diversified climate-resilient income generating activities and nature-based solutions as natural resources management plans (including community forest management plans).

The scope of the assignment is anchored in Component 2 (Resilient livelihoods and sustainable landscape management) of the TRALARD II project, and the Consultant will work in collaboration with relevant project and district teams to carry out the following functions amongst others:

  • Conduct a capacity needs assessment of the proposed community groups and community champions, and design incubation and readiness program tailored to group needs;
  • Develop a criteria framework to assess the investment readiness of community groups that are under the incubation programme;
  • In collaboration with the Camp Extension Officers, Forestry Department and District Teams, facilitate development of nature-positive proposal for community groups and community champions, and initiate the Community Forest Management processes and raise awareness;
  • Deliver training sessions for the community groups (using participatory and practical approaches);
  • Capacity Development of Community Champions to enhance their capacity to strengthen the local entrepreneurial ecosystem;
  • Provide technical backstopping during the incubation period, including coaching and mentorship, and develop a monitoring and evaluation framework to track progress and document lessons.
  • Engage and involve relevant Government staff, and other key stakeholders, from the national, provincial and district level in capacity building programs to promote knowledge transfer and sustainability.

The shortlisting criteria for the firm will be as follows;

  1. Have at least 10 years’ experience in design and implementation of sustainable landscape management and community-based market driven and value chain development projects;
  2. Demonstrate extensive experience in supporting (a) community mobilization, (b) community forest management, (c) strengthening governance and leadership of community groups, (d) business finance, rural finance, and/or micro–finance, (e) nature-positive investments and livelihoods associated with NbS and climate change adaptation, (f) rural local business incubation and (d) capacity development of local stakeholders and members of the communities;
  3. Track record of successfully running effective incubation programmes;
  4. Proven experience in managing business incubation programs specifically tailored to the Zambian context will be an added advantage.
  5. Proven experience in the target districts will be an added advantage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Sixth Edition, February 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant’s Qualification and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method as set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Sixth Edition, February 2025

The Ministry of Green Economy and Environment now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and / or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

Further information can be obtained from the address below during office hours (08:00 hours to 13:00 hours and 14:00 hours to 17:00 hours local / Zambian time).

Expression of Interest should be addressed to:

The Permanent Secretary,

Ministry of Green Economy and Environment

P.O. Box 30147

LUSAKA, ZAMBIA

The deadline for submission of expression of interest is Thursday, 18th June 2026 at 17:00 hours local / Zambian time.

INSTITUT NATIONAL DE LA STATISTIQUE

ETABLISSEMENT PUBLIC A CARACTERE ADMINISTRATIF

DIRECTION GENERALE

PROJET D’HARMONISATION ET D’AMELIORATION DES STATISTIQUES EN AFRIQUE DE L’OUEST ET DU CENTRE (PHASAOC) - CREDIT IDA 73140 NE 182, rue de la Sirba - BP 13416 Niamey - NIGER • Tél. : (227) 20 72 35 60 • Fax : (227) 20 72 21 74 • https://www.ins.ne • E-mail : ins@ins.ne

 

AVIS DE SOLLICITATIONS DE MANIFESTATION D’INTERET

 

RECRUTEMENT D’UN CONSULTANT INTERNATIONAL EN VUE DE L’APPUI A LA RENOVATION DE L’INDICE DU COUT DE LA CONSTRUCTION (ICC) AU NIGER.

 

  1. CONTEXTE ET JUSTIFICATIONS 

 

Dans le cadre de l’amélioration continue du Système statistique national, l’Institut National de la Statistique (INS) du Niger a engagé des actions visant à renforcer la qualité, la pertinence et la régularité de production des statistiques économiques conjoncturelles.

 

À ce titre, l’INS envisage la rénovation de l’Indice du Coût de la Construction (ICC), afin de disposer d’un indicateur actualisé, fiable et conforme aux normes et bonnes pratiques internationales en matière d’indices statistiques. En effet, l’ICC actuellement disponible présente des limites tenant, entre autres, à l’obsolescence de son année de base, à l’évolution du secteur de la construction, à l’adaptation insuffisante du panier de biens et services, ainsi qu’à la nécessité de renforcer les procédures techniques de collecte, de traitement, de calcul et de diffusion.

 

Au regard de la technicité de cette opération, l’INS entend recourir aux services d’un consultant international individuel disposant d’une expérience confirmée en matière de mise en place, de rénovation ou d’harmonisation des indices de prix ou d’activité, notamment dans les pays africains membres d’AFRISTAT.

 

  • Les présents Termes de Référence sont élaborés en vue du recrutement dudit consultant individuel.
  1. OBJET ET OBJECTIFS DE LA MISSION :

Objet : La présente mission a pour objet le recrutement d’un consultant international individuel chargé d’apporter un appui technique et méthodologique à l’INS pour la rénovation de l’Indice du Coût de la Construction (ICC) au Niger.

Objectif général :

L’objectif général de la mission est d’appuyer l’INS du Niger à mettre en place un ICC rénové, robuste, pertinent, documenté et exploitable, conformément aux standards méthodologiques en vigueur, notamment ceux d’AFRISTAT.

Objectifs spécifiques :

- réaliser un diagnostic du dispositif actuel de production de l’ICC ;

- proposer un cadre conceptuel et méthodologique révisé pour l’ICC ;

- appuyer la définition de l’année de base, de la structure de pondération et du panier de l’indice ;

- accompagner l’élaboration ou la révision des outils de collecte et de contrôle qualité ;

- appuyer la conception des procédures de traitement, de calcul, d’analyse et de diffusion de l’ICC ;

- renforcer les capacités des cadres de l’INS sur l’ensemble du dispositif ;

- appuyer l’élaboration d’un manuel ou guide pour la production régulière de l’ICC rénové.

 

 

  1. LESRESULTATS ATTENDUS

 

- un diagnostic complet du dispositif actuel de production de l’ICC est disponible ;

- une méthodologie révisée et validée de l’ICC est proposée ;

- les outils de collecte, de supervision et de contrôle sont élaborés ou mis à jour ;

- les procédures de traitement et de calcul sont définies et testées ;

- les cadres techniques de l’INS sont formés ;

- un manuel de procédures de production régulière de l’ICC est élaboré ;

- une feuille de route opérationnelle pour l’internalisation durable de la production de l’ICC est disponible.

 

IV. Étendue des prestations et tâches du consultant :

 

4.1. Diagnostic de l’existant

- examiner la documentation disponible sur l’ICC actuel ;

- analyser le cadre conceptuel, les sources de données, les outils de collecte, les procédures de traitement et les modalités de calcul existantes ;

- identifier les insuffisances techniques, méthodologiques et organisationnelles ;

- proposer les axes prioritaires de rénovation.

4.2. Conception méthodologique de l’ICC rénové

- définir le champ, la couverture et les unités d’observation de l’ICC ;

- proposer l’année de base appropriée ;

- définir le panier de biens, services et postes de coûts pertinents pour la construction ;

- proposer la structure de pondération ;

- recommander la formule de calcul la mieux adaptée ;

- définir les modalités de chaînage, de révision et de mise à jour éventuelle de l’indice.

4.3. Outils et procédures

- élaborer ou réviser les questionnaires, fiches et supports de collecte ;

- élaborer les manuels de l’enquêteur, du contrôleur et du superviseur ;

- proposer les règles de contrôle, d’apurement et de validation des données ;

- appuyer la mise en place des tableaux de traitement et des programmes de calcul, au besoin ;

- définir les formats de tableaux de diffusion et de publication.

4.4. Renforcement des capacités

- préparer les modules de formation ;

- animer les sessions de formation au profit des cadres de l’INS ;

- assurer le transfert de compétences aux équipes nationales ;

- formuler des recommandations pratiques pour la pérennisation du dispositif.

4.5. Accompagnement à la validation

- participer aux séances techniques de revue des livrables ;

- intégrer les observations formulées par l’INS ;

- accompagner la validation technique de la méthodologie et des outils ;

- proposer une feuille de route de mise en œuvre post-mission.

 

V. Livrables attendus et durée de la mission :

Livrables attendus :

- Rapport de démarrage, comprenant la compréhension de la mission, la méthodologie, le calendrier détaillé d’exécution et les besoins en documentation ;

- Rapport diagnostic du dispositif actuel de production de l’ICC ;

- Note méthodologique de l’ICC rénové, incluant notamment le champ, le panier, les pondérations, l’année de base, les sources, les procédures de calcul et de diffusion ;

- Projet d’outils de collecte et de manuels techniques ;

- Supports de formation et rapport de formation des cadres de l’INS ;

- Projet de manuel de procédures de production de l’ICC ;

- Rapport final de mission, intégrant les recommandations opérationnelles et la feuille de route.

 

Tous les livrables seront produits en français et transmis en version modifiable et en version PDF.

 

Durée, lieu et modalités de réalisation :

La durée prévisionnelle de la mission est de trente (30) jours, répartis entre travail à distance et missions à Niamey.

À titre indicatif, la mission pourra être exécutée selon le phasage ci-après : Phase 1 : démarrage et diagnostic ; Phase 2 : conception méthodologique et élaboration des outils ; Phase 3 : formation, finalisation des procédures et validation des livrables.

 

Le lieu principal d’exécution est Niamey, avec possibilité de travaux préparatoires ou de finalisation à distance. Le calendrier détaillé sera arrêté d’un commun accord au démarrage de la mission.

VI. Profil, qualifications et critères d’évaluation du consultant :

 

Formation :

- être titulaire au minimum d’un diplôme de niveau Bac +5 en statistique, économie, économétrie, mathématiques appliquées, ou dans tout autre domaine jugé équivalent ;

- un diplôme d’Ingénieur Statisticien Économiste ou une qualification équivalente constituera un atout.

 

Expérience générale :

- justifier d’au moins dix (10) années d’expérience professionnelle pertinente dans les statistiques économiques, les statistiques d’entreprises ou les indices conjoncturels ;

- avoir une expérience confirmée d’appui technique auprès d’instituts nationaux de statistique ou d’organismes statistiques régionaux/internationaux.

 

Expérience spécifique :

- avoir réalisé au moins deux (2) missions similaires de conception, de rénovation, d’harmonisation ou de mise en place d’indices du coût de la construction, ou d’indices apparentés ;

- avoir une expérience dans l’élaboration de guides méthodologiques, de manuels de procédures et d’outils de collecte ;

- avoir une expérience avérée dans la formation et le transfert de compétences au profit des cadres nationaux ;

- une expérience de travail dans les pays d’Afrique de l’Ouest, du Sahel ou de l’Afrique subsaharienne constituera un avantage important.

 

Compétences techniques et qualités personnelles :

- bonne maîtrise des normes et recommandations internationales relatives aux indices statistiques ;

- bonne capacité de rédaction technique en français ;

- bonne maîtrise des outils bureautiques et, au besoin, des logiciels de traitement statistique ;

- sens de l’organisation et du respect des délais ; aptitude à travailler en équipe ; rigueur, discrétion et professionnalisme.

 

Critères indicatifs d’évaluation des candidatures :

- Formation académique : 15 points

- Expérience générale pertinente : 20 points

- Expérience spécifique en indices de prix / ICC / statistiques d’entreprises : 40 points

- Expérience en formation, transfert de compétences et élaboration de manuels/guides : 15 points

- Connaissance du contexte africain, notamment Afrique de l’Ouest/Central, et qualité de la rédaction en français : 10 points

 

Le candidat classé premier, sur la base des qualifications et de l’expérience, sera invité à la négociation conformément aux règles applicables.

 

VII. Supervision, obligations et dispositions diverses :

 

Supervision et coordination :

La mission sera placée sous la responsabilité de la Direction Générale de l’INS. Le suivi technique sera assuré par la direction ou la cellule technique chargée des statistiques économiques et des prix, avec désignation d’un point focal pour la coordination opérationnelle. Le consultant travaillera en étroite collaboration avec les cadres de l’INS concernés par la production de l’ICC.

 

Obligations de l’INS :

L’INS mettra à la disposition du consultant la documentation disponible relative à l’ICC, les données et informations jugées nécessaires à la mission, un cadre de travail approprié pendant les séjours à Niamey, l’organisation des séances techniques avec les équipes concernées, ainsi que les observations sur les projets de livrables dans des délais raisonnables.

 

Obligations du consultant :

Le consultant est tenu d’exécuter la mission conformément aux présents Termes de Référence, de respecter le calendrier convenu, de produire des livrables de qualité, d’observer la confidentialité des données et informations mises à sa disposition, et de céder à l’INS les droits d’usage sur l’ensemble des documents élaborés dans le cadre de la mission.

 

Confidentialité, impartialité et conflits d’intérêts :

Le consultant retenu devra faire preuve d’indépendance, d’impartialité et de neutralité dans l’exécution de sa mission. Il s’engage à préserver la confidentialité de toutes les informations auxquelles il aura accès et à signaler toute situation de conflit d’intérêts réel ou potentiel.

 

Dossier de candidature :

Les candidats intéressés devront fournir au minimum :

- une lettre de manifestation d’intérêt signée ;

- un curriculum vitae détaillé, daté et signé, faisant ressortir les expériences pertinentes ;

- les copies des diplômes et attestations utiles ;

- les références de missions similaires réalisées ;

- une offre technique succincte présentant la compréhension de la mission et l’approche proposée ;

- une offre financière ou proposition d’honoraires, si requis dans le dossier de consultation.

 

 

Prise en charge :

La prise en charge de cette activité sera assurée par le « Projet d’Harmonisation et d’Amélioration des Statistiques de l’Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre » (PHASAOC), financement Banque Mondiale (BM), conformément au budget prévisionnel ci-dessous.

 

Méthode de sélection et dépôt des plis : Le dossier devra être composé des pièces suivantes :

 

  • Une lettre de manifestation d’intérêt signée ;
  • Un curriculum vitae détaillé, daté et signé, faisant ressortir les expériences pertinentes ;
  • Les copies des diplômes et attestations utiles ;
  •  Les références de missions similaires réalisées ;
  • Une offre technique succincte présentant la compréhension de la mission et l’approche proposée ;

 

Les dossiers de candidature doivent être déposés au plus tard le 17 juin 2026 à 10 H00, heure locale de Niamey (TU+1) :

  • Soit sous plis fermés à l’INSTITUT NATIONAL DE LA STATISTIQUE (INS) Projet d’Harmonisation et d’Amélioration des Statistiques en Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre (PHASAOC) BP : 13 416 Niamey – Niger Téléphone : (227) 20 72 35 60.
  • Soit envoyés par email (format PDF) à l’adresse suivante : Email : aribrahim@ins.ne ; avec copie à : iamadou@ins.ne; ari2006_toubo@yahoo.fr;  yaboubacar@ins.ne ;

Dans le cas où les candidatures sont communiquées sous plis fermés, les dossiers doivent être envoyés dans une enveloppe format A4 portant l’intitulé de l’AMI.

Le Consultant sera sélectionné en accord avec les procédures définies dans le « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets (FPI) » Révision de Septembre 2023 puis en février 2025.

Il reste entendu que le recrutement d’un candidat fonctionnaire doit satisfaire aux dispositions de la clause 3.23 d) du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets (FPI) » Révision de Septembre 2023, puis en février 2025.

procnotices.notice_text:
GENERAL PROCUREMENT NOTICE

 

 

INDIA

MAHARASHTRA URBAN WATER SUPPLY SANITATION & REUSE PROGRAM

Water Supply Sanitation & Wastewater Management

GENERAL PROCUREMENT NOTICE

Loan No./Credit No./TF No./Grant No.

Project ID No. P514088

 

 

The Government of Maharashtra intends to apply for financing in the amount of US$ 500 million equivalent from the World Bank toward the cost of the Maharashtra Urban WSS & Reuse Program, and it intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments for goods, works, non-consulting services and consulting services to be procured under this project. This project will be jointly financed by the Government of Maharashtra.

 

The project will include the following components

  1. Wastewater Collection & Treatment
    1. Expand sewerage network infrastructure & provide household sewer connections
    2. Construct new STPs and augment existing STP capacity
    3. Upgrade systems to meet discharge norms
  2. Water Supply & Sanitation Service Improvement
    1. Improve distribution systems for better coverage
    2. Reduce non-revenue water (NRW)
    3. Strengthen operation & maintenance systems
    4. Upgrade existing infrastructure for efficiency
  3. Reuse of treated wastewater
    1. Develop infrastructure for reuse (pipelines, offtake systems) under DBOT model
    2. Supply treated wastewater to industries and establish systems for reuse-based revenue generation
    3. Promote reuse for non-potable applications
  4. Sludge Management & Circular Economy
    1. Treat and process sludge from STPs
    2. Convert sludge into fertilizer/soil conditioner
    3. Generate energy (biogas) from sludge
  5. Institutional Strengthening of ULBs
    1. Build capacity for project planning and implementation
    2. Strengthen O&M practices within ULBs
    3. Develop asset management systems & implement cost recovery mechanisms
  6. Financial Structuring & Private Capital Mobilization
    1. Structure PPP projects (DBOT/annuity models)
    2. Raise funds through bonds (pooled/singular) and borrowings by leveraging blended finance (public + private)

 

Procurement of contracts financed by the World Bank will be conducted through the procedures as specified in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (July 2016 revised September 2025) (Procurement Regulations), and is open to all eligible firms and individuals as defined in the Procurement Regulations. After project negotiations, the World Bank shall arrange the publication on its external website of the agreed initial procurement plan and all subsequent updates once it has provided a no objection.

 

Specific procurement notices for contracts subject to open international competitive procurement will be announced, as they become available, on the World Bank’s external website and www.mahatenders.org.

Interested eligible firms and individuals who would wish to be considered for the provision of goods, works, non-consulting services and consulting services for the above-mentioned project, or those requiring additional information, should contact the Borrower at the address below:

5th Floor, Nirmal bhavan, Near CR2 mall, Nariman Point
Mumbai – 400032

Avis d’Appel d’Offres pour Fournitures

Équipement des IA et des IEF en Matériels informatiques

 et de reprographie

 

Appel d’Offres No: SN-MEN-542835-GO-RFB/F_PAPSE_213

Projet : Projet d’Amélioration des Performances du Système Educatif (PAPSE)

Acheteur : Ministère de l’Education nationale

Pays : Sénégal

Intitulé du Marché : Équipement des IA et des IEF en matériels informatiques et de reprographie

Crédit No : Crédit IDA 70440-SN ; P169916

Emis le : 1er juin 2026

 

1. Le gouvernement du Sénégal a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour financer le Projet d’Amélioration des Performances du Système Educatif (PAPSE) du Ministère de l’Education nationale (MEN), et à l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce financement pour effectuer des paiements au titre du Marché « Équipement des IA et des IEF en matériels informatiques et de reprographie ».

L’Emprunteur utilisera la méthode de décaissement par Paiement Direct, telle que définie dans les Directives de Décaissement de la Banque mondiale pour le Financement de Projet d’Investissement, à l’exception des paiements pour lesquels le marché prévoit l’utilisation de crédit documentaire. 

2. Le Ministère de l’Education nationale dans le cadre du Projet d’Amélioration des Performances du Système Educatif (PAPSE) sollicite des offres fermées de la part de soumissionnaires éligibles et répondant aux qualifications requises, en un (01) lot unique et indivisible, pour fournir  et livrer  les équipements informatiques, de reprographie et de projection à savoir : 75 ordinateurs de bureau ; 95 ordinateurs portables ; 75 imprimantes multifonctions (impression, scan, copie) ; 75 Imprimantes numériques de production; 75 Vidéoprojecteurs et 75 Onduleurs.

A cet effet, les exigences en matière de qualification sont :

  • Expérience : avoir réalisé au moins deux (02) marchés similaires d’un montant égal au moins à quatre cent soixante-quinze mille (475 000 000) F CFA au cours des cinq (05) dernières années (2025, 2024, 2023, 2022 et 2021). Le soumissionnaire doit joindre les attestations de bonne exécution avec les copies des contrats de marchés et les procès-verbaux de réception signés par les administrations ou services bénéficiaires.
  • Capacité financière:     
  • Etats financiers:

Le soumissionnaire doit fournir des états financiers certifiés ou, si la loi du pays du Soumissionnaire ne l’exige pas, d’autres états financiers acceptables pour l’Acheteur, pour les trois (3) dernières années (2022, 2023 et 2024) démontrant la solidité actuelle de la situation financière de l’entreprise.

  • Attestation de ligne de crédits:

Le soumissionnaire doit soumettre une lettre délivrée par une banque attestant que le soumissionnaire dispose de fonds propres, de liquidités ou bénéficiera d’un crédit, dont le montant sera au moins égal à trois cent soixante-quinze millions (375 000 000) Francs CFA (XOF) ou son équivalent dans une devise convertible.

  • Capacité financière:

Le Soumissionnaire doit prouver, documentation à l’appui qu’il satisfait aux exigences de capacité technique ci-après :

ü fournir dans l’offre technique une description détaillée (prospectus, ou catalogue édité en français émanant du fabriquant) des articles proposés conformément à la spécification technique,

ü fournir l’autorisation du fabriquant dument signée par le fabriquant,

ü disposer d’un service après-vente (SAV) performant et opérationnel pour une période d’une année au moins après la réception définitive des équipements. A ce titre, le soumissionnaire doit disposer d’un  personnel technique qualifié capable d’assurer le SAV, comprenant :

  • trois (03) ingénieurs IT avec 05 ans d’expérience ;
  • deux (02) techniciens en maintenance.

 Les curriculums vitae (CV) du personnel proposé doivent être joints à l’offre.

3. La passation du Marché sera conduite par Mise en Concurrence nationale (AON) tel que défini dans le « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement » de la Banque mondiale daté du 1er Juillet 2016 révisé en septembre 2025.

4. Les soumissionnaires éligibles et intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations auprès du bureau de PAPSE au 2ème étage de l’immeuble CAC à Yoff, Cité Biagui, route de l’aéroport Léopold Sédar Senghor, Sénégal ou par courriel envoyé à l’adresse électronique : bm.papse@education.sn et prendre connaissance des documents d’Appel d’offres durant les heures de bureau de 9h30 à 16h00 GMT à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessus.

5. Les soumissionnaires intéressés et éligibles peuvent obtenir gratuitement le Dossier d’Appel d’Offres complet en langue française en formulant une demande écrite à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessus ou à l’adresse électronique suivante : bm.papse@education.sn

6. Les offres devront être soumises à l’adresse suivante au bureau des marchés du PAPSE au 2ème étage de l’immeuble CAC à Yoff, Cité Biagui, route de l’aéroport Léopold Sédar Senghor au plus tard le lundi 20 juillet 2026 à 10 heures GMT.

7. La soumission des offres par voie électronique ne sera pas autorisée. Les offres remises en retard ne seront pas acceptées. Les offres seront ouvertes publiquement en présence des représentants des Soumissionnaires et de toute personne choisissant d’être présente à la Salle de conférence du PAPSE au 2èmeétage de l’immeuble CAC à Yoff, Cité Biagui, route de l’aéroport Léopold Sédar Senghor, le lundi 20 juillet 2026 à 10 heures GMT.

8.  Toutes les offres doivent comprendre une Garantie de l’Offre, sous forme de garantie bancaire délivrée par une banque internationale réputée ou organisme de garantie, située dans un pays éligible d’un montant de quatorze millions cinq cent mille (14 500 000) francs CFA (XOF) ou équivalent en devise convertible.

REPUBLIQUE DEMOCRATIQUE DU CONGO

MINISTERE DE L’EDUCATION NATIONALE ET NOUVELLE CITOYENNETE

Avis d’Appel d’Offres National

TRAVAUX DE CONSTRUCTION DE QUATRE ECOLES A DEKESE 2, 3 et 4 DANS LA PROVINCE DU KASAI

Projet : Projet d’Apprentissage et d’Autonomisation des Filles en RDC-PAAF

Intitulé du Marché : Travaux de Construction de quatre écoles à Dekese 2,3 et 4 dans la Province du KASAI

Crédit No : Crédit IDA N° 7284 – ZR

Emis le : mardi 02 juin 2026

Date limite : jeudi 02 juillet 2026 à 15 h00 (heure de Kinshasa)

1. Le Gouvernement de la République Démocratique du Congo (DRC) a obtenu de la Banque Mondiale (BM) à hauteur d’USD 400 millions le financement du Projet d’Apprentissage et d’Autonomisation Des Filles (PAAF), et à l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce financement pour effectuer des paiements au titre du Marché N° ZR-PAAF-544769-CW-RFB relatif aux Travaux de Construction de quatre écoles à Dekese 2,3 et 4 dans la Province du KASAI.

2. Le Projet d’Apprentissage et d’Autonomisation Des Filles (PAAF) sollicite des offres fermées de la part de soumissionnaires éligibles et répondant aux qualifications requises pour exécuter les travaux de construction de quatre écoles à Dekese 2,3 et 4 dans la province du Kasaï.

3. La procédure sera conduite par mise en concurrence nationale en recourant à un Appel d’Offres (AO) telle que définie dans le « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement » de la Banque mondiale (Juillet 2016, révisée en Novembre 2017, Juillet 2018, Novembre 2020, Septembre 2023 et Septembre 2025), et ouverte à tous les soumissionnaires des pays éligibles tels que définis dans le Règlement de passation des marchés.

4. Les Soumissionnaires éligibles et intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations auprès du Projet d’Apprentissage et d’Autonomisation Des Filles (PAAF) du Ministère de l’Education Nationale et Nouvelle Citoyenneté à l’adresse courriel suivante : paafrdcpm@gmail.com en réservant copie à ECP_PAAF@PAAF.CD;  Téléphone : 00 (243) 999997349 et prendre connaissance du dossier d’Appel d’offres, de 9 heures à 15 heures à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous :  72, Avenue Uvira ; Immeuble Robem Tower, 6 ème étage , Commune de la Gombe – Kinshasa, RDC (Référence : Grand Hôtel Pullman).

5. Les soumissionnaires intéressés peuvent obtenir un Dossier d’Appel d’Offres complet en langue française en formulant une demande écrite à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous contre un paiement non remboursable de cinquante dollars américains (50 $US) ou l’équivalent dans une monnaie convertible. La méthode de paiement sera paiement par virement bancaire (MIN FIN/PAAF-INTERETS CREDITEURS & DAO N° 00011050233200236968721 USD/Code Swift : BCDCCDKIXXX).

Le document d’Appel d’Offres sera remis en électronique (PDF non modifiable et Word sur flash disk) au soumissionnaire contre présentation de la preuve de paiement.

6. Les offres devront être soumises à l’adresse ci-dessous au plus tard le jeudi 02 juillet 2026 à 15 h00 (heure de Kinshasa. La soumission des offres par voie électronique « ne sera pas » autorisée. Toute offre arrivée après l’expiration du délai limite de remise des offres sera écartée. Les enveloppes marquées « OFFRE ORIGINALE » seront ouvertes en présence des représentants des soumissionnaires et des personnes présentes à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous jeudi 02 juillet 2026 à 16 h00 (heure de Kinshasa).  

7. L’attention est attirée sur le Règlement de Passation de Marchés exigeant que l’Emprunteur divulgue des informations sur la propriété effective du Soumissionnaire retenu, dans le cadre de la Notification d’Attribution du Marché, en utilisant le Formulaire de Divulgation des Bénéficiaires Effectifs tel qu’il est inclus dans le document d’appel d’offres.

8. Toutes les offres doivent comprendre une Déclaration de Garantie d’Offre.

9. L’adresse à laquelle il est fait référence ci-dessus est :

A l'attention de :  Madame Alice MUTAMBAYI, Coordonnatrice Déléguée du PAAF.

Adresse : Avenue Uvira, n°72, Immeuble Robem Tower, 6è étage, Commune de la Gombe/Référence Grand Hôtel Pullman

Ville : Kinshasa

procnotices.notice_text:
SOLICITAÇÃO DE MANIFESTAÇÃO DE INTERESSE
SERVIÇOS DE CONSULTORIA
BRASIL – Ministério do Meio Ambiente e Mudança do Clima - MMA
Paisagens Sustentáveis da Amazônia - ASL BRASIL 2
Acordo de Doação N.º TF0B6898-BR – Banco Mundial
Número de Referência: BR-FGV-554854-CS-INDV

 

ESCOPO

Contratação de consultor individual especializado em silvicultura tropical e ecologia voltados ao diagnóstico ambiental e levantamento de campo para a caracterização precisa do estágio de degradação florestal nas Unidades de Conservação estaduais, provendo subsídios técnicos para a modelagem de estratégias de restauração ecológica e a identificação de espécies nativas potenciais adequadas às especificidades do bioma amazônico, no âmbito do Projeto Paisagens Sustentáveis da Amazônia (ASL Brasil – Fase 2).

 

O Beneficiário recebeu uma doação do Banco Mundial para a execução do Projeto PAISAGENS SUSTENTÁVEIS DA AMAZÔNIA FASE 2 – ASL BRASIL 2 de nº TF0B6898-BR. O Projeto tem como principal objetivo promover a gestão integrada da paisagem e a conservação de ecossistemas terrestres e de água doce em áreas específicas, a fim de melhorar o manejo e a conectividade de Áreas Protegidas na Região Amazônica

.

Solicitação de Manifestação de Interesse – SMI Nº 008/2026

 

A FUNDAÇÃO GETÚLIO VARGAS torna público que está aberto o prazo para consultores individuais elegíveis, interessados(as) na apresentação de MANIFESTAÇÃO DE INTERESSE, com vistas à prestação dos serviços detalhados no Termo de Referência, disponível em: https://asl-brasil.fgv.br/compras-e-contratacoes, devendo demonstrar que são qualificados(as) e possuem experiência para desempenhar tais serviços.

As manifestações de interesse deverão ser enviadas até o dia 12/06/2026, às 23h59, para o e-mail asl2.compras@fgv.br, identificadas como:

“SMI Nº 008/2026 –Estágio de Degradação Florestal – Antimary.

”

OBJETIVO

Contratar consultor individual especializado para a realização de diagnóstico ambiental e caracterização do estágio de degradação em áreas situadas na Floresta Estadual do Antimary e Floresta Estadual do Afluente, visando subsidiar tecnicamente a priorização das intervenções de restauração ecológica, a definição de estratégias e métodos adequados de recomposição da vegetação nativa, mediante integração de informações técnicas, levantamentos de campo e apoio de imageamento.

 

ESCOPO DOS SERVIÇOS

· Levantamento e sistematização de informações técnicas e ambientais das áreas amostrais;

· Definição de critérios, parâmetros e indicadores para classificação dos estágios de degradação e sucessão vegetal;

· Planejamento metodológico para seleção e refinamento das áreas amostrais;

· Apoio técnico ao imageamento aéreo com utilização de VANTs para reconhecimento das áreas;

· Levantamento florístico e estrutural em parcelas delimitadas nas áreas selecionadas;

· Caracterização da composição, diversidade e densidade de espécies florestais;

· Identificação de fatores de degradação ambiental e potencial de regeneração natural;

· Integração de dados obtidos em campo e por imageamento para qualificação das análises ambientais;

· Definição de espécies nativas potenciais para futuros projetos de restauração ecológica;

· Consolidação de relatório técnico contendo diagnóstico ambiental, classificação do estágio de degradação florestal e proposição de estratégias e métodos de restauração ecológica adequados às condições locais.

 

REQUISITOS MÍNIMOS DE QUALIFICAÇÃO

· Graduação em áreas como Engenharia Florestal, Engenharia Agronômica, Ciências Ambientais, Ciências Biológicas, Ecologia e áreas correlatas;

· Experiência profissional em atividades relacionadas à silvicultura aplicada a espécies nativas voltadas ao bioma amazônico;

· Experiência em identificação de espécies nativas e processos de sucessão ecológica;

· Experiência em levantamentos florísticos, coleta de dados dendrométricos e análise estrutural da vegetação;

· Experiência em projetos de restauração ecológica e/ou monitoramento ambiental na Amazônia;

· Conhecimento em geoprocessamento e técnicas de sensoriamento remoto aplicadas à análise ambiental;

· Domínio de ferramentas estatísticas e de sistematização de dados técnicos e ambientais.

 

DOCUMENTAÇÃO PARA MANIFESTAÇÃO DE INTERESSE

· Currículo atualizado;

· Comprovação de formação acadêmica;

· Comprovação de experiência profissional;

· Portfólio ou relação de trabalhos executados, quando aplicável.

 

INFORMAÇÕES ADICIONAIS

Esta Solicitação de Manifestação de Interesse não pressupõe qualquer compromisso de contratação. A seleção observará o Regulamento de Aquisições para Mutuários de Operações de Financiamento de Projetos de Investimento do Banco Mundial, edição de setembro de 2023.

 

CONTATOS

Informações adicionais poderão ser solicitadas pelo endereço eletrônico: asl2.compras@fgv.br.

 

Rio de Janeiro, 25 de maio de 2026.

 

Maurício Wanderley Estanislau da Costa

Gerente de Procurement – FGV Projetos / ASL Brasil 2

procnotices.contact_organization: Ministry of Health, Social Welfare and Gender Affairs (Tuvalu)
procnotices.notice_text:
Request for Expressions of Interest

(Consultant Services, Individual)

This position is intended for a National Consultant

 

Country:  Tuvalu  

Project: Pacific Healthy Islands Transformation Project (PHIT) and Tuvalu Health System Strengthening Project (THSSP)

Assignment Name: Administrative and Clerical Officer (National)

Grant/Credit/Loan: E528-TV & E0860-TV

Project ID:  P508550 & P175170

Activity Reference: TV-TV-MOH-549388-CS-INDV

 

 

  1. Project Background

The World Bank financed Pacific Healthy Islands Transformation (PHIT) Project is a regional initiative covering Tonga, Kiribati, Fiji and Tuvalu, designed to increase access to quality health services across participating Pacific Island countries, with emphasis on non-communicable disease (NCD) management and primary health care (PHC) strengthening. In Tuvalu, these regional PHIT activities are being implemented alongside the national Tuvalu Health System Strengthening Project (THSSP).

 

The Tuvalu Health System Strengthening Project (THSSP) is an IDA funded national initiative (USD 15 million) designed to improve the availability and quality of essential health services in Tuvalu. THSSP supports expansion of Princess Margaret Hospital’s physical and human resource capacity, strengthens delivery of primary health care with a focus on non-communicable disease (NCD) prevention and management at the clinics.

 

To coordinate implementation of THSSP and the PHIT activities, MOHSW has established a Project Management Unit (PMU). The PMU requires a full-time national Administrative and Clerical Officer to provide front-office, administrative, clerical, logistical and record-keeping support to ensure efficient implementation and operations across both projects in Tuvalu. The Officer will work under the PMU Project Manager / PHIT Coordinator and will closely support PMU technical, financial and M&E staff, including the Project Accountant and Deputy Project Manager based in Funafuti.

 

 

 

  1. OBJECTIVE

The primary objective of the Administrative and Clerical Officer is to provide timely, reliable and confidential administrative and clerical support to the PMU to facilitate smooth implementation of THSSP and PHIT activities in Tuvalu. The Officer will manage front-office functions, office logistics, document and records management, basic financial administration support, coordination of travel and events, and communication and filing systems to meet MOHSW and World Bank requirements. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following link:

https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/5idgo6zpyxfo191tampfw/Admin-ToR-1.docx?rlkey=tzk4ag0ju4t8jgio9zk82hcww&st=cbdu8767&dl=0

 

3) INVITATION

The Project Management Unit (PMU) on behalf of the Implementing Agency now invites eligible individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services.

Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (attach curriculum vitae with description of experience in similar assignments, similar conditions, three references, etc.).

 

4)EVALUATION CRITERIA

The criteria for selecting the Consultant are:

 

  1. Education.

•        Minimum: High school diploma.

•        Desirable: Certificate in office administration, secretarial studies, bookkeeping or computing.

 

  1. Experience.

•        Minimum: At least 3 years’ relevant administrative/clerical experience, preferably in a government, health sector, project/PMU or donor-funded environment.

 

  1. Skills and Knowledge.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English and Tuvaluan.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office suite (Word, Excel, Outlook) and basic competency with electronic filing systems; familiarity with simple database or accounting filing preferred.
  • Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, ability to prioritize multiple tasks and meet deadlines with minimal supervision.
  • Professional client service orientation, confidentiality, discretion and integrity.
  • Ability to work effectively in a multicultural, multi-agency team and adapt to changing work demands.
  • Basic numeracy and record-keeping skills; ability to assist in financial document preparation for Withdrawals and audits.

 

The attention of interested Consultants (including firms) is drawn to paragraph 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers July 2016, revised in November 2017 (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Expressions of Interest must be delivered to surieli16@gmail.com with copy to peletefakaola@gmail.com not later than 12th June, 2026 at 17:00pm.

procnotices.notice_text:
SOLICITAÇÃO DE MANIFESTAÇÃO DE INTERESSE
SERVIÇOS DE CONSULTORIA
BRASIL – Ministério do Meio Ambiente e Mudança do Clima - MMA
Paisagens Sustentáveis da Amazônia - ASL BRASIL 2
Acordo de Doação N.º TF0B6898-BR – Banco Mundial
Número de Referência: BR-FGV-552477-CS-INDV

 

 

ESCOPO

Contratação de consultor individual especializado em geoprocessamento aplicado ao sensoriamento remoto para realização de análises espaciais e produção de mapas temáticos voltados à identificação, delimitação, caracterização e priorização de áreas com potencial para regeneração natural assistida nas Florestas Estaduais do Gregório, da Liberdade, do Mogno e na Área de Relevante Interesse Ecológico Japiim Pentecoste.

 

O Beneficiário recebeu uma doação do Banco Mundial para a execução do Projeto PAISAGENS SUSTENTÁVEIS DA AMAZÔNIA FASE 2 – ASL BRASIL 2 de n° TF0B6898-BR. O Projeto tem como principal objetivo promover a gestão integrada da paisagem e a conservação de ecossistemas terrestres e de água doce em áreas específicas, a fim de melhorar o manejo e a conectividade de Áreas Protegidas na Região Amazônica.

 

Solicitação de Manifestação de Interesse – SMI Nº 004/2026

 

A FUNDAÇÃO GETÚLIO VARGAS, torna público que está aberto o prazo para consultores individuais elegíveis interessados(as) na apresentação de MANIFESTAÇÃO DE INTERESSE, com vistas à prestação dos serviços detalhados no Termo de Referência, disponível em: https://asl-brasil.fgv.br/compras-e-contratacoes, devendo demonstrar que são qualificadas e têm a experiência para desempenhar tais serviços.

As manifestações de interesse deverão ser enviadas até o dia 12/06/2026, às 23h59, para o e-mail asl2.compras@fgv.br, identificadas como “SMI Nº 004/2026 – Consultoria em Geoprocessamento (Regeneração-Gregório/Liberdade/Mogno/Japiim)”.

asl2.compras@fgv.br

 

OBJETIVO

Contratar consultor individual especializado para realizar análises espaciais e produzir mapas temáticos voltados à identificação, delimitação, caracterização e priorização de áreas com potencial para regeneração natural assistida nas Florestas Estaduais do Gregório, da Liberdade, do Mogno e na Área de Relevante Interesse Ecológico Japiim Pentecoste.

 

ESCOPO DOS SERVIÇOS

  • Levantamento, compilação e organização de bases de dados geoespaciais multiescala;
    Integração e padronização de dados ambientais e cartográficos em ambiente SIG;
    Análise espacial e interpretação de imagens de satélite de alta resolução;
    Classificação de uso e cobertura do solo aplicada à análise ambiental;
    Identificação, delimitação e caracterização de áreas com potencial para regeneração natural assistida;
  • Produção de mapas temáticos e bases geoespaciais compatíveis com sistemas de informação geográfica;
  • Consolidação de relatório técnico contendo síntese das análises espaciais realizadas e priorização das áreas identificadas.

 

REQUISITOS MÍNIMOS DE QUALIFICAÇÃO

  • Graduação em áreas como: Geografia, Engenharia Florestal, Ciências Ambientais, Ecologia, Geoprocessamento e áreas correlatas.
  • Experiência comprovada em trabalhos de geoprocessamento, gestão de dados e análises ambientais e geoespaciais;
  • Experiência comprovada em sensoriamento remoto aplicado à análise territorial e ambiental;
    Experiência comprovada em análise de dinâmica de uso e cobertura do solo;
    Experiência comprovada na elaboração de mapas temáticos e análises de dados geoespaciais aplicados à gestão ambiental;
  • Domínio de ferramentas de Sistemas de Informação Geográfica (SIG) e análise espacial.

 

DOCUMENTAÇÃO PARA MANIFESTAÇÃO DE INTERESSE

  • Currículo atualizado;

ESCOPO

 

Contratação de consultor individual especializado na realização de diagnóstico socioambiental voltado à identificação e caracterização do perfil dos ocupantes do entorno das áreas mapeadas e, quando aplicável, no interior das Unidades de Conservação, como potenciais para a condução da regeneração natural nas Unidades de Conservação Floresta Estadual do Antimary e Floresta Estadual do Afluente, no âmbito do Projeto Paisagens Sustentáveis da Amazônia (ASL Brasil – Fase 2).

 

O beneficiário recebeu uma doação do Banco Mundial para a execução do Projeto PAISAGENS SUSTENTÁVEIS DA AMAZÔNIA FASE 2 – ASL BRASIL 2 de n° TF0B6898-BR. O Projeto tem como principal objetivo promover a gestão integrada da paisagem e a conservação de ecossistemas terrestres e de água doce em áreas específicas, a fim de melhorar o manejo e a conectividade de Áreas Protegidas na Região Amazônica.

 

Solicitação de Manifestação de Interesse – SMI Nº 005/2026

 

A FUNDAÇÃO GETÚLIO VARGAS torna público que está aberto o prazo para CONSULTORES INDIVIDUAIS elegíveis, interessados(as) na apresentação de MANIFESTAÇÃO DE INTERESSE, com vistas à prestação dos serviços detalhados no Termo de Referência, disponível em: https://asl-brasil.fgv.br/compras-e-contratacoes, devendo demonstrar que são qualificados(as) e têm experiência para desempenhar tais serviços.

 

As manifestações de interesse deverão ser enviadas até o dia 12/06/2026, às 23h59, para o e-mail asl2.compras@fgv.br, identificadas como: SMI Nº 005/2026 – Diagnóstico Socioambiental (Antimary/Afluente)”.

 

OBJETIVO

Contratar consultor individual especializado para realização de diagnóstico socioambiental voltado à identificação e caracterização do perfil dos ocupantes do entorno das áreas previamente mapeadas como potenciais para a condução da regeneração natural nas Unidades de Conservação Floresta Estadual do Antimary e Floresta Estadual do Afluente.

 

ESCOPO DOS SERVIÇOS

  • Levantamento e sistematização de informações socioambientais e territoriais;
  • Planejamento metodológico e definição de instrumentos de coleta de dados;
  • Realização de levantamento de campo junto aos ocupantes do entorno das áreas selecionadas;
  • Identificação e caracterização do perfil socioambiental, econômico e produtivo dos ocupantes;
  • Levantamento de informações sobre uso e ocupação da terra, práticas produtivas e dependência de recursos naturais;
  • Aplicação de entrevistas semiestruturadas, formulários padronizados e observação direta;
  • Integração das informações coletadas com dados secundários e geoespaciais;
  • Consolidação de relatório técnico contendo análise das dinâmicas socioambientais locais e subsídios para definição de estratégias de restauração e adequação ambiental.

 

REQUISITOS MÍNIMOS DE QUALIFICAÇÃO

  • Graduação em áreas como: Engenharia Florestal, Engenharia Agronômica, Ciências Ambientais, Ciências Biológicas, Ecologia e áreas correlatas.
  • Experiência comprovada em levantamentos socioambientais e/ou socioeconômicos em áreas rurais;
  • Experiência comprovada em análise ambiental integrada ao contexto socioambiental;
  • Experiência comprovada em trabalhos relacionados ao uso e ocupação da terra e práticas produtivas;
  • Experiência comprovada na sistematização de dados primários e secundários e elaboração de relatórios técnicos;
  • Experiência em processos participativos, entrevistas e atividades de campo junto a comunidades locais.

procnotices.notice_text:
1. INVITATION TO QUOTE.

 

Date: 1 June 2026

 

To:

 

Dear Supplier,

 

1.1 You are invited to submit your price quotation for the Aquaculture Goods and Equipment (Component 3).

 

1.2 The Government of Tuvalu has received a Grant from the World Bank towards the cost of the Tuvalu Pacific Regional Oceanscape Program for Economic Resilience (PROPER) and intends to apply the proceeds of this grant to eligible payments under the contract for which this Request for Quotation is issued.

 

1.3 You must quote for all (100%) the items under this Invitation.

 

1.4 You shall submit by e-mail the Price Quotation with the Form of Quotation in accordance with the requirements specified in paragraph (9) below and addressed to:

 

Name: Samuelu Telii

Title: Project Coordinator

Project: Tuvalu Pacific Regional Oceanscape Program for Economic Resilience

Email Address: samuelut@tuvalufisheries.tv OR propertuv@tuvalufisheries.tv

 

Where forms are required to be signed, scanned copies of the signed forms should be attached in the email.

 

1.5 Your quotation in English language should be accompanied by adequate technical documentation and catalogue(s), or pertinent information for each quoted item.

 

1.6 The deadline for receipt of your quotation(s) by the Purchaser at the address indicated in Paragraph 4 is: 15 June, 2026 before close of business 4:00pm, Tuvalu time.

1.7 The evaluation of the price quotations will be conducted through procedures for RFQ as set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, November 2020, which can be accessed from the World Bank website Procurement-Regulations.pdf (worldbank.org)

1.8 Quotations by electronic means are acceptable.

 

1.9 Your quotation should be submitted as per the following instructions and in accordance with the attached Contract. The attached Terms and Conditions of Supply is an integral part of the Contract. Incomplete or partial Quotations not filled out according to the instructions may be rejected. Alternative quotations/options are not allowed.

 

1.10 Your quotation should include the following:

 

    1. Completed and signed Form of Quotation (Attachment 1); and

 

    1. Completed and signed Terms and Conditions of Supply (Attachment 3); and

 

    1. Completed and signed Compliance Statement (Attachment 4) demonstrating substantial responsiveness of the goods offered to the technical specification required, along with any technical documentation and/or catalogues of proposed products;

 

    1. Priced and signed Bill of Quantities (Attachment 5 – Excel file). The prices should be quoted for delivery CIP Funafuti for imported goods according to INCOTERMS, 2020. Prices may be quoted in any single freely convertible currency.  Prices should not include custom duties, excise-duty, and custom procedures tax in the Republic of Tuvalu. Prices quoted shall be fixed and not subject to any adjustment during contract performance.

 

             2. EVALUATION OF QUOTATIONS:

2.1 Offers determined to be substantially responsive to the technical specifications will be evaluated by comparing the evaluated price.

 

2.2   The Purchaser will determine for each item the evaluated price, by adjusting the price quotation by making any correction for any arithmetical errors as follows:

 

      1. Where there is a discrepancy between amounts in figures and in words, the amount in words will govern.
      2. Where is a discrepancy between the unit rate and the line item total resulting from multiplying the unit rate by the quantity, the unit rates as quoted will govern.
      3. If a Supplier refuses to accept the correction, his quotation will be rejected.

2.3 Prices quoted will be evaluated for all items together and the contract awarded to the bidder offering the lowest evaluated total price of all items.

 

2.4 For comparison of evaluated prices, the total evaluated price for all items will be converted to Australian Dollars at the selling rate of exchange prevailing on the deadline date for submission of quotations as issued by the ANZ bank.

 

3.  AWARD OF CONTRACT:

3.1 A Contract will be awarded to the bidder offering the lowest evaluated price for all items, and which technically compliant with the required specifications. The successful participant will sign a Contract as per attached Form of Contract and Terms and Conditions of Supply.

 

4.  VALIDITY OF THE OFFER:

 

4.1 Your quotation(s) should be valid for a period of sixty [60] days from the deadline for receipt of quotation(s) indicated in Paragraph 6 of this Request for Quotation.

 

4.2 Further information can be obtained from:

Title: Procurement Officer

Project: Tuvalu Pacific Regional Oceanscape Program for Economic Resilience

Email Address: reenam@tuvalufisheries.tv OR propertuv@tuvalufisheries.tv

4.4 A prospective bidder requiring any clarification of the Request for Quotation shall contact the Purchaser in writing (email) at the Purchaser’s address specified in the Paragraph 4.9. The Purchaser will notify all invited bidders of any request for clarification and the response, provided that any such request is received no later than two (2) calendar days prior to the deadline for receiving of quotes.

 

4.5 At any time prior to the deadline for receiving of quotes, the Purchaser may amend the Request for Quotation by issuing an addendum. Any addendum issued shall be part of the Request for Quotation and shall be communicated in writing to all who have obtained the Request for Quotation directly from the Purchaser.

 

4.6 The bidder shall bear all costs associated with the preparation and submission of its quote, and the Purchaser shall not be responsible or liable for those costs, regardless of the conduct or outcome of the bidding process.

 

4.7 The Purchaser reserves the right to accept or reject any quote, and to annul the bidding process and reject all quotes at any time prior to contract award, without thereby incurring any liability to bidders.

4.8  At the time the Contract is awarded, the Purchaser reserves the right to increase or decrease the quantity of goods, provided this does not exceed fifteen (15) percentage per item, and without any change in the unit prices or other terms and conditions of the quote and the Request for Quotation.

 

4.9 Please confirm by e-mail the receipt of this invitation and whether or not you will submit the price quotation(s).

 

 

 

Yours sincerely,

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT)

ALBANIA

BUILDING RESILIENT BRIDGES PROJECT (BRBP)

Project ID No.: P174595

Loan No.:  94790-AL

Assignment Title: PIT-Site Engineer (south region)  

Reference No. Ref.:AL-ARA-551786-CS-INDV

Recruitment Type: Local Recruitment

The Government of Albania has received a loan in the amount of 51.6 million EUR financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Building Resilient Bridges Project (BRBP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for individual consulting services, subject of this request for expressions of interest (REoI).  

Albanian Road Authority (ARA) will be responsible for implementation of the BRBP with the support of a Project Implementing Team (PIT) within ARA.

The individual consultant will serve as the Site Engineer (hereinafter referred to as “Engineer”) for the BRB Project. The Engineer will be an integral part of the Project Implementation Team (PIT) housed at the ARA. The Engineer will be responsible for offering technical expertise and support, taking on the primary role of ensuring the successful execution of all engineering activities and any other activities that require the Engineer's specialized knowledge throughout the implementation of the BRB Project.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website https://www.arrsh.gov.al/njoftime-brbp

The Albanian Road Authority now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Candidates should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and be able to demonstrate previous experience as Site Engineer as follows:

  • University degree in Civil Engineering or related field
  • A minimum of five (5) years of relevant working experience as an engineer in transport sector, preferably in road and/or bridge projects. Previous           ,      experience in projects financed by the World Bank or other international financial institutions, would be considered an advantage.
  • The candidate must be computer literate, with proficiency in computer software operations (AutoCAD, Microsoft Word, Excel, Power-Point, MS Project,       and database management, etc.)
  • Excellent Knowledge of English and Albanian language (in speaking and writing)

Applicants that fulfill the qualification requirements will be further evaluated based on the below criteria: 

  1. General Qualification – 30 points
  2. Adequacy for the assignment – 60 points
  3. Language – 10 points

This is a full-time position for one (1) year, extendable for the duration of the project. The position is renewable annually based on the business needs, performance, and mutual agreement. The successful candidate for the Site Engineer position should be available to commence immediately upon completion of the contract award procedure. 

The interested candidates will be selected in accordance with the Open Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants (IC) method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (Procurement Regulations), in investment project financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services November 2020.

Further information can be obtained during office hours 08:00 to 16:30 (Monday to Thursday) and 08:00 to 14:00 on Fridays at the address given below.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below in person, or by mail, or by e-mail by June 17, 2025, at 16:00 hrs. local time.

procnotices.bid_description: Coordinador del proyecto
procnotices.contact_organization: Centro de Investigación y Educación Sexual y Reproductiva
procnotices.notice_text:
Lugar de Trabajo: Santa Cruz

    FORMACIÓN

    • Licenciatura en Ciencias Sociales.
    • Estudio de post grado o diplomado en Gestión de Proyectos.
    • Estudio de post grado o diplomado en Educación, Derechos Sexuales y/o Derechos Reproductivos.

    COMPETENCIAS TÉCNICAS

    • Manejo de recursos didácticos y preparación de materiales educativos para jóvenes y adolescentes.
    • Manejo de Metodologías participativas para adolescentes y jóvenes.
    • Conocimiento de la Ley 348 Para garantizar a las mujeres una vida libre de Violencia.
    • Conocimiento de la Ley Avelino Siñani.
    • Conocimiento de la Sentencia Constitucional 0206/2014.
    • Conocimiento del Modelo de Atención Integral De Adolescentes.
    • Conocimiento de Normativas Relacionadas con el ejercicio de los Derechos de adolescentes y jóvenes con énfasis en Derechos Sexuales y Derechos Reproductivos.
    • Diseño, seguimiento, monitoreo y evaluación de proyectos.
    • Enfoque de género, generacional intercultural e interseccional.
    • Manejo de herramientas tecnológicas.
    • Manejo avanzado de Microsoft Office.
    • Ingles Intermedio.

    EXPERIENCIA

    • General de 5 años.
    • Específica de 3 años.
    • En trabajo en ONGs y/o en organizaciones con cooperación internacional.
    • En trabajo con organizaciones sociales y redes de jóvenes.
    • En gestión de proyectos.
    • En trabajos con perspectiva de género, participación comunitaria, interculturalidad e interseccionalidad.
    • En trabajo en el tema de violencia de género, desde un enfoque multisectorial y con un enfoque centrado en la sobreviviente, que garantice prácticas seguras, éticas y alineadas con estándares internacionales.
    • En manejo y aplicación de metodologías y técnicas participativas para grupos de jóvenes y adolescentes.
    • Con temas referentes a Derechos Humanos y Derechos Sexuales y Derechos Reproductivos, género e interculturalidad e interseccionalidad.

    COMPETENCIAS BLANDAS

    • Liderazgo
    • Trabajo en ambientes multidisciplinarios y multiculturales
    • Trabajo con equipos a distancia
    • Capacidad de comunicación efectiva
    • Gestión por resultados
    • Proactividad
    • Compromiso con la protección a niños/as, adolescentes y jóvenes.

    OTROS

    • Certificado de Antecedentes de la FELCC. (presentación posterior)

procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION)

 

Country: Pakistan
Project: Digital Economy Enhancement Project
Credit No.: 75140-PK
Assignment Title: Selection of Project Coordinator
Reference No.: PK-MOITT-548479-CS-INDV

 

1.          The Government of Pakistan has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Digital Economy Enhancement Project (DEEP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for procuring the subject consulting services, which shall be implemented by the Ministry of IT and Telecom (MoITT) through its Project Management Unit (PMU).

 

2.          The consulting services (“the Services”) include the professional expertise of a “Project Coordinator” on a monthly lump sum remuneration basis. The Ministry of IT and Telecom, through the Project Management Unit, intends to hire the services of a “Project Coordinator” for DEEP to assist the project management in the relevant field. The consultant, as an expert in the field, will provide quality advice maintaining the highest degree of integrity and ethical standards. The individual consultant will be hired initially for a period of 24 months.

 

3.          The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below or can be downloaded from https://njp.gov.pk/.

 

4.          The Ministry of IT and Telecom, through its Project Management Unit, invites eligible candidates (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services as “Project Coordinator” for the Digital Economy Enhancement Project. Interested candidates should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the expected Services. The shortlisting criteria are based on qualifications, relevant experience, and additional skills as outlined in the Terms of Reference.

 

5.          The selected candidate will be required to present original documents at the time of credentials verification. Submission of any false information will lead to immediate disqualification of the candidate at any stage of the hiring process.

 

6.          The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

7.          A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Open Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

8.          Further information may be obtained from the Senior Procurement Specialist at procurement.specialist@deep.moitt.gov.pk during 10:00 AM – 3:00 PM (Pakistan Standard Time) on any working day until the deadline for submission of expressions of interest.

 

9.          Expressions of interest must be submitted online at https://njp.gov.pk/ by June 1, 2026.

 

10.        The address referred to above is:
